We need propose a retrosynthesis route with 1 reaction for target SMILES: [CH2:1]=[C:2]([c:3]1[cH:4][cH:5][cH:6][cH:7][cH:8]1)[C@@H:9]1[CH2:10][CH2:11][CH2:12][C@@:13]1([OH:14])[C:15]([F:16])([F:17])[F:18]

Interpret: It's an alkene attached to phenyl and a cyclopentanol with CF3? Actually C15 with three Fs attached to carbon 15? The SMILES: C(F)(F)F attached to carbon 15 which is attached to carbon 13? Let's rewrite: The core is a cyclopentane (C9-10-11-12-13) with OH on C13, and CF3 attached to C15 which is attached to C13? Actually [C:15]([F:16])([F:17])[F:18] is a carbon with three Fs (CF3) attached to C13? The SMILES shows [C@@H:9]1[CH2:10][CH2:11][CH2:12][C@@:13]1([OH:14])[C:15]([F:16])([F:17])[F:18]. So C9 is chiral carbon attached to cyclopentane ring (C9 is part of ring?), Actually C9 is attached to ring: C9 is attached to C10 (CH2), which goes to C11, C12, then C13 (chiral) which has OH and attached to CF3 carbon (C15). So it's a cyclopentanol with CF3 substituent.

The alkene part: [CH2]=[C]([c1ccccc1]) attached to C9? Actually the SMILES: [CH2:1]=[C:2]([c:3]1[cH:4][cH:5][cH:6][cH:7][cH:8]1)[C@@H:9]... So the alkene carbon C2 is attached to phenyl and to C9 (the chiral carbon). So overall it's an allylic alkene attached to phenyl and to cyclopentanol.

The guidance: carbonyl-ene reaction retrosynthesis: forward reaction is carbonyl-ene: carbonyl + alkene -> allylic alcohol (product). So retrosynthetic step: break the C-O bond to give a carbonyl (ketone) and an alkene (with allylic hydrogen). So we need to propose a precursor: a ketone (probably a cyclopentanone with CF3) and an alkene (phenyl-substituted alkene) that undergo carbonyl-ene to give the product.

Thus the retrosynthetic step: target -> precursors: (1) phenyl-substituted alkene (maybe styrene?) Actually the product has alkene between CH2 and C (attached to phenyl and C9). In carbonyl-ene, the alkene is the same as product's alkene? The product's alkene is formed from the original alkene? Wait carbonyl-ene: alkene + carbonyl -> new C-C bond, new C-O bond (hydroxyl) at allylic position, and the double bond shifts. In product we have an allylic alcohol (OH on carbon adjacent to double bond). In our target, OH is on cyclopentane, not on the alkene carbon. The carbonyl-ene likely formed the C-O at the carbonyl carbon (now OH) and formed new C-C bond between alkene carbon and carbonyl carbon. So the precursor carbonyl is a ketone attached to cyclopentane (maybe cyclopentanone with CF3). The alkene is a phenyl-substituted alkene (styrene) that will undergo ene with the ketone to give the product where the new bond is between the alkene carbon (C2) and the carbonyl carbon (C9). The OH ends up on carbonyl carbon (now C13? Actually carbonyl carbon becomes the carbon bearing OH after reaction). In product, OH is on C13 which is part of cyclopentane, not the carbonyl carbon? Wait carbonyl carbon is part of cyclopentanone (C13). After ene, the carbonyl carbon becomes an alcohol (C13 OH). So yes.

Thus precursor: cyclopentanone with CF3 at carbon adjacent to carbonyl? The product has CF3 attached to C15 which is attached to C13 (the carbonyl carbon). In precursor, the carbonyl carbon (C13) is attached to CF3 carbon (C15) as same. So precursor is CF3-substituted cyclopentanone (maybe 2-(trifluoromethyl)cyclopentanone). The carbonyl carbon is C13, attached to CF3 carbon (C15). So precursor: O= C13 (carbonyl) attached to CF3 carbon (C15) and to the rest of ring.

Thus we need to find a template that does carbonyl-ene retrosynthesis. Use search_template_catalog_by_criteria with functional_groups_broken: ["C-C double bonds", "ketones"] and formed: ["aliphatic hydroxyls", "five-membered rings"] maybe. Already attempted but got empty. Could be because target SMILES not correct. Let's try using a simpler SMILES without atom mapping: "C= C(c1ccccc1)C1CCCC1C(=O)C(F)(F)F". That's a ketone version. Use search.
